stories.title: Trump’s H-1B crackdown is starting to drive tech talent back to India, China
stories.summary: Tightening US H-1B visa rules under the Trump administration have caused many Indian and Chinese tech workers to leave the US and return home due to job insecurity and visa uncertainties. The number of H-1B visa approvals and tech job opportunities in the US is declining amid layoffs, hiring freezes, and stricter immigration policies, squeezing foreign professionals out. Returnees to India and China face mixed prospects: India offers some tech jobs but with lower pay, while China’s booming tech sector attracts top talent back from the US. BENGALURU/BEIJING – When Deepak left the United States in May with his wife and two children, he was effectively dismantling a life he had built over the last 15 years to return to India. Even though he found another tech-related job shortly after he was laid off in October, Deepak ultimately decided to exchange the uncertainty triggered by President Donald Trump’s wide-ranging immigration crackdown for the relative certainty in his home country. At least in India, he would not have to be anxious about his right to remain if he failed to secure another job within 60 days after getting laid off, like he was sweating over his H-1B temporary work visa in the US. At a time when the Trump administration is only looking to further limit immigration, foreigners like Deepak have been thrown into limbo by these ever-changing and tightening regulations. Under Trump, it is also more expensive and cumbersome for American employers to recruit skilled foreigners. “When Trump announced the US$100,000 (S$128,000) application fee for new H-1B visas, it created a lot of confusion. Companies were not sure if it applied to renewals, transfers as well as new hires,” said Deepak, 44, who requested anonymity for fear of reprisals. Deepak is a pseudonym. Eventually, it became clear that the proposed US$100,000 fee was for new H-1B applications, which would have been 25 times the prevailing fee.

stories.title: Iran parliament speaker says US used more firepower in Iran than on Vietnam
stories.summary: Iran parliament speaker says US used more firepower in Iran than on Vietnam Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said the US had used more firepower against Iran than during the Vietnam War. Speaking at an event broadcast by state broadcaster IRIB, Ghalibaf said Tehran must reach a “point of deterrence” to avoid becoming trapped in a cycle of war and peace.
